title: Legal structures
examples: What is the difference between a sole trader and a partnership?
When should a business become a limited company?
How does liability affect choosing a business structure?

explain.say: Today we are looking at different business structures. These structures affect how a business is run. We will learn about sole traders first.
A sole trader is owned and run by one person. This person has total control over all decisions. For example, a local baker might start as a sole trader.

draw.text: Sole Trader: One owner, full control

explain.say: Next we look at a partnership. This structure involves two or more people working together. For example, two friends opening a small design agency form a partnership.
A limited company is a separate legal entity. This means the owners are not personally responsible for debts. For example, a large tech firm might register as a limited company.
Liability is a key concept we must understand. It refers to the legal responsibility for the business's debts. In a sole trader, your personal assets are at risk.

items: Sole Trader: Personal assets at risk

explain.say: In a limited company, the owners' personal assets are usually protected. This separation limits their financial risk greatly. This is called limited liability.

items: Sole Trader: Personal assets at risk

faq.q: What is the main difference in risk between a sole trader and a limited company?
faq.a: With a sole trader, your personal assets are at risk if the business fails. A limited company usually protects your personal assets from business debts.
asks: Does a sole trader risk everything?
Are personal assets safe in a limited company?

faq.q: Does a partnership mean all partners share the same risk?
faq.a: In a partnership, partners usually share responsibility and risk together. This means they are jointly accountable for the business's debts.
asks: What happens to risk in a partnership?

faq.q: Why would someone choose a limited company over a sole trader?
faq.a: People often choose a limited company for protection. It legally separates the owners from the business's debts, which is safer.
asks: What is the benefit of being limited?
When is a limited company better?

faq.q: Is it always better to be a limited company?
faq.a: No, limited companies involve more rules and paperwork. A sole trader is simpler to set up initially.
asks: Are there downsides to limited companies?

faq.q: What is the legal status of a partnership?
faq.a: A partnership is a legal agreement between two or more people to run a business together. They share profits and losses.
asks: Is a partnership a legal arrangement?

facts: A sole trader is owned and run by one individual.
Partnerships involve two or more people sharing ownership.
Limited companies are separate legal entities from their owners.
In a sole trader, the owner has unlimited liability.

quiz.say: If a business fails, which structure usually puts the owner's personal savings at risk?
quiz.why: The sole trader structure means the owner's personal assets are directly linked to the business debts.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the main benefit of a limited company is that it separates personal assets from business debts.
wrong.1: This is incorrect because the key difference lies in the level of personal protection offered by the structure.
wrong.3: This is tempting because partners share risk, but it is not always the owner's personal savings that are at risk.

quiz.say: Which structure offers the strongest protection for the owners' private money?
quiz.why: A limited company is legally separate, meaning its debts are generally not the personal debts of the owners.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the owner of a sole trader is personally responsible for all business debts.
wrong.1: While it offers some separation, partners often face joint and several liability, risking personal assets.
wrong.2: This is incorrect because both structures expose the owners to a higher degree of personal financial risk.

quiz.say: If two people start a business together, what is the most common structure they might use?

options.show: Both Sole Trader and Limited Company
options.say: Both Sole Trader and Limited Company

quiz.why: A partnership is specifically designed for two or more people to share ownership and profits.

wrong.1: This is wrong because a sole trader must be one person, not two or more.
wrong.2: This is too complex for a simple start; a partnership is often the first step before forming a limited company.
wrong.3: This is impossible because the structure must fit the number of owners involved.
